Diversion is a free-to-play platformer produced by Ezone.com for iOS and Android platforms. I've played this game on iPad Air 2 and several Samsung Galaxy devices, so the review will include all of them.

Diversion is a deceptively simple game where you literally do almost nothing but jump. Your character moves along a semi-randomized field while you jump to avoid obstacles, collect gems and power-ups, and to reach the end of the stage. The game is broken up into several fields, each with 30 stages that are tied together thematically in design and obstacles. You beat stages to unlock more stages and collect gems to buy outfits for your character. Each stage has an outfit that will double the total number of gems you collect at the end though, so in practice they are more utility than they are customization. There is also an infinite run mode that will randomly spawn tiles based on a theme for as long as you can keep yourself from falling to your doom. There are the vestiges of a story there, but the game itself doesn't seem too interested in it.

Overall, the game's simple mechanics work decently well. Sometimes the obstacles aren't immediately clear, but repetition fixes that. There are the occasional bugs, and sometimes the set pieces don't work together perfectly. That can be frustrating, but it doesn't happen often enough for me to consider it a critical issue. Except in the infinite run mode. Sometimes the set pieces end up screwing you over completely by putting you into impossible circumstances. Not 'oh god, this jump is too hard' impossible. Legitimately cannot progress because you are given the tools you need to succeed impossible. Lower end devices will also see the game lag horrendously on some of the more complex stages, especially where you have to do long flights.

Another major bug is in the monetization, and this one is huge, bordering on false advertising and critical enough that it made me stop playing. You can buy gems and little tokens that are basically continues. That's fine. They also run static image ads occasionally on the loading screen between levels. That's also fine. The game offers to remove advertising if you make any purchase on their store. That's lovely of them. It doesn't work, at least on iOS. That is intolerable. If you make a promise, you follow through.

Overall, the game is fine. Cutsie graphics, mostly playable, easy to understand, easy to pick up and put down. I cannot recommend it because of their blatant false statements, but if it weren't for that, I would say to give it a go.
